crackedness_criteria.name: Academic Excellence & Rigor
crackedness_criteria.description: Measures GPA, coursework difficulty, academic honors, and intellectual horsepower demonstrated through formal education at Stanford or comparable institutions.

scoring_guide.high: GPA 3.9+ with honors distinctions (e.g., Tau Beta Pi), highly technical double major or demanding single major, evidence of graduate-level coursework or research publications listed on Google Scholar. Demonstrates exceptional academic ceiling.
scoring_guide.medium: GPA 3.5–3.89 or strong GPA in a rigorous single major, relevant coursework in CS/engineering/economics, no major academic honors but solid performance in demanding curriculum.
scoring_guide.low: GPA below 3.5 or unspecified, limited coursework rigor, no academic distinctions, or academic record that does not stand out relative to the Stanford peer group.

crackedness_criteria.name: Technical & Analytical Skill Depth
crackedness_criteria.description: Measures the depth and breadth of hard skills — programming languages, quantitative methods, research tools, and domain-specific technical competencies that signal ability to build or analyze at a high level.

scoring_guide.high: Proficient in multiple programming languages (e.g., Python, C++, MATLAB, SQL) AND demonstrates applied use in real projects or research. Has quantitative modeling, ML/AI, or financial engineering skills evidenced by concrete outputs (repos, papers, deployed tools).
scoring_guide.medium: Competent in 1–2 relevant technical areas with some applied experience, but depth is narrower or application is more coursework-based than project/industry-based.
scoring_guide.low: Minimal technical skills listed, no evidence of applied technical work, or skills are generic and not substantiated by projects or experience.

crackedness_criteria.name: Entrepreneurial Initiative & Builder Mindset
crackedness_criteria.description: Measures whether the candidate has taken initiative to create something — a startup, product, research project, club, or venture — beyond assigned coursework or internships.

scoring_guide.high: Has founded or co-founded a startup, launched a product with real users/revenue, led a significant independent research initiative, or built something from zero with measurable impact. Participation in accelerators (e.g., Stanford Climate Ventures Accelerator) with active project counts strongly.
scoring_guide.medium: Has participated in hackathons, led a student organization, contributed meaningfully to an early-stage project, or taken on a leadership role in an entrepreneurial context without full founding credit.
scoring_guide.low: No evidence of self-initiated projects or entrepreneurial activity beyond standard coursework; primarily a consumer of opportunities rather than a creator.

crackedness_criteria.name: Professional Experience Quality & Trajectory
crackedness_criteria.description: Measures the prestige, relevance, and growth trajectory of internships, research roles, or full-time experience. Evaluates whether the candidate is accelerating and landing increasingly competitive opportunities.

scoring_guide.high: Internships or research roles at top-tier firms (FAANG, leading VC/PE, elite fintech, top research labs), with clear upward trajectory and substantive contributions (not just task completion). Evidence of repeat offers, promotions, or expanding scope.
scoring_guide.medium: Solid internship or research experience at reputable organizations with some demonstrated impact, but either at mid-tier firms or with less evidence of standout performance or trajectory.
scoring_guide.low: Limited professional experience, roles at less competitive organizations, or experience that appears peripheral with no clear narrative of growth or increasing responsibility.

crackedness_criteria.name: Leadership & Outsized Impact
crackedness_criteria.description: Measures whether the candidate has led teams, organizations, or initiatives and created impact beyond themselves — scaling their influence through others or through systems they built.

scoring_guide.high: Held formal leadership positions (president, founder, team lead, PI-level research) with quantifiable outcomes (members grown, revenue generated, papers published, users acquired). Impact clearly extends beyond individual contribution.
scoring_guide.medium: Some leadership experience (committee lead, project manager, team member with leadership responsibilities) but impact is more localized or outcomes are less clearly quantified.
scoring_guide.low: No meaningful leadership roles or impact is entirely individual with no evidence of multiplying effort through others.

crackedness_criteria.name: Intellectual Curiosity & Cross-Domain Thinking
crackedness_criteria.description: Measures whether the candidate demonstrates genuine curiosity that crosses disciplinary boundaries — combining technical, economic, scientific, and humanistic thinking in ways that signal original thought.

scoring_guide.high: Pursues genuinely interdisciplinary work (e.g., biomedical computation + economics, CS + energy science, AI + finance) with evidence that the combination produces novel insights or projects. Engages with ideas outside their primary field in a substantive way.
scoring_guide.medium: Dual major or minor that suggests breadth, or coursework spanning multiple domains, but the cross-pollination hasn't yet produced distinctive outputs or a clear intellectual identity.
scoring_guide.low: Narrowly focused on a single domain with no evidence of curiosity beyond core requirements; intellectual profile is conventional for their major.

fit_criteria.name: Fintech or Economics Domain Knowledge
fit_criteria.description: Measures direct knowledge of financial technology, financial systems, economic theory, or markets — through coursework, research, projects, or work experience specifically in these domains.

scoring_guide.high: Has dedicated coursework in economics, finance, or fintech AND has applied this knowledge in a real context (fintech internship, economics research with publication/presentation, financial modeling project, startup in the space). The candidate can hold a substantive conversation with a VC about market structure, financial products, or economic mechanisms.
scoring_guide.medium: Has relevant coursework (e.g., economics major or minor, finance electives) or one tangential work experience in a financial context, but has not yet deeply applied this knowledge in a project or professional setting.
scoring_guide.low: Minimal or no coursework, research, or experience in fintech or economics. Domain knowledge appears incidental rather than intentional.

fit_criteria.name: Startup or VC Ecosystem Exposure
fit_criteria.description: Measures familiarity with the startup and venture capital ecosystem — through accelerators, VC internships, startup employment, founder networks, or entrepreneurship programs.

scoring_guide.high: Has worked at a VC firm, been part of a startup accelerator (e.g., Stanford Climate Ventures Accelerator), founded a venture-backed or revenue-generating company, or has a clear track record of engaging with the startup ecosystem in a substantive role. Understands how VCs think about deals, markets, and founders.
scoring_guide.medium: Has attended startup events, participated in pitch competitions, worked at an early-stage company in a non-founding role, or taken entrepreneurship coursework — but hasn't yet had deep VC or founder-level exposure.
scoring_guide.low: No meaningful exposure to the startup or VC ecosystem. Background is primarily academic or corporate with no signal of interest in or understanding of venture-backed company building.

fit_criteria.name: Quantitative & Financial Modeling Capability
fit_criteria.description: Measures the candidate's ability to work with financial data, build economic models, or apply quantitative methods to financial or economic problems — a core skill for both fintech builders and economists.

scoring_guide.high: Has built financial models, conducted econometric analysis, worked with market data, or applied ML/statistical methods to financial problems in a research or professional context. Can speak credibly about valuation, risk, or economic measurement.
scoring_guide.medium: Has relevant coursework in statistics, econometrics, or financial mathematics, and some project-based application, but hasn't yet applied these skills in a high-stakes professional or research context.
scoring_guide.low: No evidence of quantitative financial or economic modeling. Technical skills exist but have not been directed toward financial or economic problems.

fit_criteria.name: Clarity of Fintech/Economics Vision or Thesis
fit_criteria.description: Measures whether the candidate has a clear, articulated perspective on a problem in fintech or economics they want to solve or study — signaling they will be an engaged, value-adding dinner participant.

scoring_guide.high: Resume or profile reveals a coherent narrative around a specific fintech problem (e.g., financial inclusion, DeFi infrastructure, payments, credit markets) or economics research question. The candidate has a point of view, not just credentials. This person will ask sharp questions at the dinner.
scoring_guide.medium: Some thematic focus is visible (e.g., interest in climate finance, healthcare economics, or emerging markets) but it's not yet fully developed into a clear thesis or problem statement.
scoring_guide.low: No discernible focus or thesis in fintech or economics. Interests appear scattered or the candidate has not yet developed a perspective on what they want to work on in this space.

fit_criteria.name: Network & Relationship Value for the Room
fit_criteria.description: Measures whether the candidate brings a network, perspective, or background that adds value to the dinner conversation and to other attendees — including geographic diversity, industry connections, or unique vantage points.

scoring_guide.high: Has connections to fintech hubs (Chicago, SF, NYC), has worked with or for notable figures in finance or tech, brings a unique geographic or demographic perspective (e.g., emerging market experience, non-traditional background), or has a public profile (research, writing, open-source) that makes them known in the community.
scoring_guide.medium: Has some relevant connections or a moderately interesting background story, but network value is primarily local (Stanford) or not yet differentiated from the typical Stanford CS/Econ student.
scoring_guide.low: Network and background are largely undifferentiated from peers; unlikely to bring a unique perspective or connection that enriches the dinner conversation beyond their individual credentials.

metadata.focus_area: Fintech startup founders and economics-focused candidates for a VC+Founders Dinner; prioritizes candidates who combine technical depth with financial/economic domain knowledge and startup ecosystem engagement
